headline: OpenAI won't go public until its models are safe, says CEO
summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated the company will delay its IPO to avoid Wall Street pressure, prioritizing confident safety claims for its rapidly advancing AI models.
details: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman confirmed the company has no firm timeline for an IPO, stating it won't happen until they can make confident safety claims about their AI models. He expressed concerns about additional pressure from Wall Street during this critical phase of AI development.

Altman's comments follow months of controversy regarding AI control, including reports of an unreleased OpenAI model hacking a rival lab. Other cybersecurity incidents have also come to light at major AI companies, sparking public discussion on system risks.

He clarified that "pacing the frontier" means prioritizing safety and alignment over capabilities, rather than an outright slowdown. Altman believes going public now would be "ill-advised" during a shift to highly capable models and new safety requirements.

While acknowledging the benefits of public companies, Altman also noted it would be "bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public." The company aims to confidently scale AI without public debate over potential negative outcomes, rather than rushing to an IPO.

headline_marked: [[Gemini gives good answers]] after enabling one hidden Workspace setting
headline: Gemini gives good answers after enabling one hidden Workspace setting
summary: Connecting Gemini to Google Workspace transforms it from a generic chatbot into a personalized assistant, summarizing documents and emails across your digital life securely.
details: Many users find Gemini frustratingly generic, requiring constant context input. The key to unlocking its potential lies in a single, often overlooked setting: enabling the Google Workspace toggle in Gemini's connected apps.
This simple action grants Gemini secure access to your personal digital ecosystem, including Google Drive, Gmail, Google Keep, and Calendar. It allows the AI to 'know' you without manual data input.

With Workspace integration, Gemini can summarize key takeaways from your files, find crucial information across your emails, and use your personal history to boost productivity. It shifts from a general knowledge base to a tailored assistant.

Before this adjustment, Gemini treated every chat like a new interaction, unable to recall personal context or access your documents. This often led to tedious copy-pasting, defeating the purpose of an AI assistant.

Crucially, this integration is secure, and your personal data is not used to train the wider Gemini model. The AI refers to your content on demand, providing answers and context exclusively for your use.

Examples include asking Gemini to retrieve specific documents like a 'Swami Jewels' color stone collection or finding credit card bill details from Gmail, instantly providing due dates and amounts. It also works seamlessly with Google Keep notes.
